classification.difficultyReason: Development: the hardest demand links reading the two 2018 series, finding their combined total and expressing each series as a percentage of that total using the explicitly taught count-over-total method. Comparing combined yearly heights also requires considering both series together.

content.prompt: The column chart shows the number of actors in each theatre group each year.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 7 graph between its stem and lettered parts
spec.description: Eight paired year groups, male left and female right. Retains the title, Year and Frequency labels, arrowed axes, five-unit labelled vertical ticks, intermediate horizontal grid lines and a boxed key to the right. No vertical grid or bar-value labels are added.
spec.mathematics: Reconstruction coordinates in year order, male/female: 2014 about 25/38; 2015 about 43/30; 2016 50/45; 2017 about 43/37; 2018 20/30; 2019 about 33/18; 2020 equal columns about 38/38; 2021 about 25/48. Off-tick coordinates reproduce approximate source geometry, not new exact givens. Approved interpretations: equal numbers in 2020; greatest combined count in 2016, 95; 2018 total 50, female 60%, male 40%.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied chart is permanently visible. No totals, percentages or answer annotations are printed on it.

children.prompt: In which year did the group have:

children.label: a
children.prompt: The same number of male and female actors?

answer.worked: The male and female columns have equal heights in $2020$.
The pair of columns for $2016$ has the greatest combined height. There are $50+45=95$ actors.

children.prompt: How many actors were there in 2018?

answer.worked:
In $2018$, there are $20$ male and $30$ female actors.
$$\text{Total}=20+30=50\text{ actors}$$
